reason: Fix d>0 and split the indices into 1<=i<=a and a<i<=b. On the first part, e_i=i, so the two divisibility counts are identical. On the second part, i -> r+i is a bijection from {a+1,...,b} to the integer interval (r+a,r+b], so the count of indices with d dividing e_i is M_d(r+a,r+b), while the count of indices with d dividing i is M_d(a,b). The assumed inequality M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b) then gives the desired conclusion.
